map.简易利润表自上而下分三层：营业收入减进货成本得毛利，再减人工、房租与水电杂费等期: The simple income statement is built top-down in three layers: operating revenue minus purchase cost gives gross profit, then minus period expenses such as labour, rent and utilities gives operating profit. Cash flow uses a different definition: it ignores whether a sale occurred and looks only at whether money actually arrived. First convert revenue into actual cash inflow by the collection rate, then subtract the expenses that must be paid in cash for the period; the difference is the net operating cash flow for the period, and adding the opening cash gives the closing balance. A positive profit with negative cash flow usually means receivables are tying up funds or stock is piling up. All calculations are done locally in the browser and no data is uploaded.

map.某期营收 246000 元、进货 128000 元、人工 46000 元、房租: In one period revenue was 246,000 CNY, purchases 128,000 CNY, labour 46,000 CNY, rent 18,000 CNY and utilities 9,000 CNY, giving a book gross margin of 47.97% and operating profit of 45,000 CNY. But the collection rate was only 78%, so actual cash inflow was 191,880 CNY while cash expenses for the period were 201,000 CNY, making net operating cash flow −9,120 CNY. This is a classic case of "earning money but having none to spend", and the problem lies in receivables rather than gross margin.
map.同上数据，若把回款率从 78% 提到 92%，现金流入升至 226320 元，经: With the same figures, raising the collection rate from 78% to 92% lifts cash inflow to 226,320 CNY and turns net operating cash flow into +25,320 CNY, leaving book profit unchanged while the cash position improves markedly. Such improvements usually come from shorter payment terms, deposits or cash discounts, with no need to sacrifice gross margin.
map.两期毛利相近（约 48%），但一期现金流为正、一期为负。若负的那期库存明显上升，: Gross margin is similar in two periods (about 48%), but cash flow is positive in one and negative in the other. If stock rose clearly in the negative period, cash turned into goods; if stock was flat but receivables rose, cash turned into IOUs. The tool cannot see either item, but comparing net operating cash flow with gross margin can point to which side to investigate.
map.这里的净利润和会计口径一样吗？: Is the net profit here the same as the accounting basis?
map.不一样。本工具不考虑折旧摊销、所得税与利息，也不区分资本性支出与费用化支出，得到: No. This tool ignores depreciation and amortisation, income tax and interest and does not distinguish capital expenditure from expensed items, so it produces a simple operating-level profit. Formal ongoing bookkeeping should follow accounting standards; this result is only for quick calculation and management reference.
map.回款率应该怎么填？: How should the collection rate be filled in?
map.填写本期实际收到的现金占本期营收的比例。若客户多为月结，可用历史平均回款率估算；: Enter the share of the period's revenue actually received in cash. If most customers pay monthly, an average historical collection rate can be used; if large one-off credit sales dominate, split them by transaction before filling in, otherwise the cash-flow judgement will be distorted.
map.为什么付现支出直接用当期全额？: Why are cash expenses taken at full amount for the period?
map.工具假设采购与费用在当期全部付清，这是最保守的口径。若你有供应商账期，实际现金流: The tool assumes purchases and expenses are all settled in the period, which is the most conservative basis. If you have supplier payment terms, the actual cash outflow is smaller than this; you can first deduct the unpaid part from the purchase figure before entering it, to bring the result closer to reality.
map.输入支持负值吗？: Does the input support negative values?
map.支持。营收之外的各项填负数可用于表示退款、冲销或政府补贴冲减；最终利润与现金流会: Yes. Negative values in the non-revenue items can represent refunds, write-offs or government subsidies; the final profit and cash flow are derived by arithmetic. But do not make revenue negative - when revenue is not greater than 0 the tool prompts you to complete it rather than returning a negative statement.
